answer: Vouching cost grows with graph distance: forging one identity is cheap, faking a neighborhood is not. First condition: vote weight derives from stake locked along an endorsement path, so a sybil cluster anchored to one real member caps at that member's stake — a grove cannot pass as a forest. Second: endorsements expire unless the pair proves distinct behavior, judging peers on a knoll of verifiable history and muting accounts whose ocean of micro-transactions all trace to one wallet.
